title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of respiratory syncytial virus and human metapneumovirus ınfections in children under five years of age
abstract: UNLABELLED: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) are major causes of acute respiratory tract infections in young children and share many epidemiological and clinical characteristics. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics, outcomes, and healthcare costs associated with RSV and hMPV infections in children younger than five years of age. In this retrospective comparative cohort study, children aged 1-71 months with laboratory-confirmed RSV or hMPV infection identified by multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction were included. RSV cases identified between September 2022 and April 2023 and hMPV cases identified between September 2022 and December 2025 were included. Both outpatient and hospitalized patients evaluated at a tertiary pediatric hospital were enrolled. A total of 693 children were included, comprising 547 with RSV infection and 146 with hMPV infection. Children with hMPV infection were significantly older and more frequently had underlying comorbidities than those with RSV infection. Bronchiolitis, cough, nasal congestion, tachypnea, chest retractions, rhonchi, oxygen supplementation, inhaled therapies, corticosteroid use, and hospitalization were more common among children with RSV infection (all p 0.05). CONCLUSION: Consistent with previous studies, RSV and hMPV differed in age distribution, clinical presentation, and healthcare utilization. These data provide additional evidence from a tertiary pediatric center in Türkiye and support the generalizability of these observations across different geographic settings. WHAT IS KNOWN: • RSV and hMPV are major causes of acute respiratory tract infections in young children, but direct comparisons between these viruses remain limited. WHAT IS NEW: • In this large pediatric cohort, RSV predominantly affected younger children and was associated with more bronchiolitis, hospitalization, and supportive treatment needs, whereas hMPV was more common in older children with comorbidities and was more frequently associated with pneumonia.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the clinical characteristics, outcomes, and healthcare costs of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infections in children under five years of age. Conducted as a retrospective comparative cohort study at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Türkiye, the research included 693 children, with 547 having RSV and 146 having hMPV infections. The findings reveal that hMPV predominantly affects older children with comorbidities, while RSV is more common in younger children and associated with more severe symptoms and higher healthcare utilization. These results align with previous studies and highlight the distinct clinical profiles of RSV and hMPV. The study's limitations include its retrospective nature and single-center focus, but the data support the generalizability of the findings across different geographic settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人偏肺病毒(hMPV)是婴幼儿急性呼吸道感染的主要病因,并且在流行病学和临床特征方面有许多相似之处。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项在三级儿科医院进行的回顾性比较队列研究研究,纳入了1-71个月龄、通过多重实时聚合酶链反应(PCR)确诊的RSV或hMPV感染患儿。RSV病例的收集时间为2022年9月至2023年4月,而hMPV病例的收集时间为2022年9月至2025年12月。纳入了门诊和住院患儿。
elements_zh.methods: 纳入了通过多重实时聚合酶链反应(PCR)确诊的RSV或hMPV感染患儿。研究比较了5岁以下儿童RSV和hMPV感染的临床特征、预后及医疗费用。
elements_zh.main_results: 与RSV感染患儿相比,hMPV感染患儿年龄显著更大,且更常伴有基础合并症。支气管炎、咳嗽、鼻塞、呼吸急促、胸骨凹陷、啰音、吸氧治疗、吸入治疗、糖皮质激素使用以及住院情况在RSV感染患儿中更为常见(所有p < 0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果与以往研究一致,突显了RSV和hMPV感染在年龄分布、临床表现和医疗资源利用方面的差异。本研究为这两种病毒在婴幼儿中的不同临床特征提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为针对hMPV感染在年龄较大且伴有合并症的儿童的监测、诊断及管理策略提供依据,同时有助于指导针对RSV在年轻人群中的更有效干预措施的开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计和单中心数据,这可能影响其结果的普遍适用性。然而,这些数据来自土耳其一家三级儿科中心,支持了这些观察结果在不同地理环境中的普遍适用性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人偏肺病毒(hMPV)是婴幼儿急性呼吸道感染的主要病因,并且在流行病学和临床特征方面有许多相似之处。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项在三级儿科医院进行的回顾性比较队列研究研究,纳入了1-71个月龄、通过多重实时聚合酶链反应(PCR)确诊的RSV或hMPV感染患儿。RSV病例的收集时间为2022年9月至2023年4月,而hMPV病例的收集时间为2022年9月至2025年12月。纳入了门诊和住院患儿。
analysis_zh.methods: 纳入了通过多重实时聚合酶链反应(PCR)确诊的RSV或hMPV感染患儿。研究比较了5岁以下儿童RSV和hMPV感染的临床特征、预后及医疗费用。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与RSV感染患儿相比,hMPV感染患儿年龄显著更大,且更常伴有基础合并症。支气管炎、咳嗽、鼻塞、呼吸急促、胸骨凹陷、啰音、吸氧治疗、吸入治疗、糖皮质激素使用以及住院情况在RSV感染患儿中更为常见(所有p < 0.05)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果与以往研究一致,突显了RSV和hMPV感染在年龄分布、临床表现和医疗资源利用方面的差异。本研究为这两种病毒在婴幼儿中的不同临床特征提供了新的见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为针对hMPV感染在年龄较大且伴有合并症的儿童的监测、诊断及管理策略提供依据,同时有助于指导针对RSV在年轻人群中的更有效干预措施的开发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计和单中心数据,这可能影响其结果的普遍适用性。然而,这些数据来自土耳其一家三级儿科中心,支持了这些观察结果在不同地理环境中的普遍适用性。

title: Genomic Surveillance of Human Metapneumovirus in the United States, 2010-2025.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a significant cause of acute respiratory illness in both children and adults, yet its genomic epidemiology remains understudied compared to other respiratory viruses. METHODS: Hybrid capture and whole-genome sequencing were performed on 616 HMPV-positive specimens from 2 cohorts: the household-based HIVE study (2010-2022) in Michigan and the multicenter IVY network (2022-2025) of hospitalized adults. Consensus sequences were generated using IRMA, clades were annotated using Nextclade, and phylogenetic trees were constructed separately for HMPV-A and HMPV-B using IQ-TREE and TreeTime. Analysis of selection by dN/dS was performed using SLAC. RESULTS: We obtained complete genomes from 325 specimens. Our analyses revealed the continued predominance of the A2.2.2 clade and little geographic structure in the United States. Genomic diversity was highest in the glycoprotein (G); we identified a shift from variants bearing the 180nt duplication to ones with a 111nt duplication. Phylogenetic analyses supported the duplication-deletion model for the origin of the duplications. The conserved fusion (F) protein showed limited antigenic variation and low rates of nonsynonymous substitutions. CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore the utility of enhanced genomic surveillance for understanding HMPV evolution and informing vaccine development. There was little genomic diversity in vaccine-targeted epitopes.
authors: Investigating Respiratory Viruses in the Acutely Ill (IVY) Network

title: Explainable AI for sentiment analysis of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) using XLNet
abstract: The outbreak of Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) in China, which later spread to the UK and other countries, raised significant public concern due to its potential impact on vulnerable populations. While HMPV typically causes mild symptoms, its effects on the elderly and immunocompromised individuals prompted health authorities to emphasize preventive measures. Moreover, continuous monitoring of respiratory viruses like HMPV remains important, as new factors (such as emerging variants) could alter their behavior over time. These factors have led to mixed public reactions, with some individuals expressing anxiety while others exhibit carelessness regarding the virus. This paper explores how sentiment analysis can enhance our understanding of public reactions to HMPV by analyzing data from social media platforms like YouTube. It highlights the importance of tracking public sentiment-ranging from fear to trust-to guide health messaging, inform policies, address misinformation, and encourage compliance with preventive measures during outbreaks. This study focuses on the use of sentiment analysis to understand public reactions to HMPV during the 2024 outbreak. The research applies advanced transformer models, particularly XLNet, achieving an accuracy of 93.50% in sentiment classification tasks. Additionally, We incorporate explainable AI (XAI) through SHAP to provide transparency in how the model identifies key factors influencing public sentiment.

source_records.abstract: The outbreak of Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) in China, which later spread to the UK and other countries, raised significant public concern due to its potential impact on vulnerable populations. While HMPV typically causes mild symptoms, its effects on the elderly and immunocompromised individuals prompted health authorities to emphasize preventive measures. Moreover, continuous monitoring of respiratory viruses like HMPV remains important, as new factors (such as emerging variants) could alter their behavior over time. These factors have led to mixed public reactions, with some individuals expressing anxiety while others exhibit carelessness regarding the virus. This paper explores how sentiment analysis can enhance our understanding of public reactions to HMPV by analyzing data from social media platforms like YouTube. It highlights the importance of tracking public sentiment-ranging from fear to trust-to guide health messaging, inform policies, address misinformation, and encourage compliance with preventive measures during outbreaks. This study focuses on the use of sentiment analysis to understand public reactions to HMPV during the 2024 outbreak. The research applies advanced transformer models, particularly XLNet, achieving an accuracy of 93.50% in sentiment classification tasks. Additionally, We incorporate explainable AI (XAI) through SHAP to provide transparency in how the model identifies key factors influencing public sentiment.

source_body_en: The outbreak of Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) in China, which later spread to the UK and other countries, raised significant public concern due to its potential impact on vulnerable populations. Moreover, continuous monitoring of respiratory viruses like HMPV remains important, as new factors (such as emerging variants) could alter their behavior over time. This paper explores how sentiment analysis can enhance our understanding of public reactions to HMPV by analyzing data from social media platforms like YouTube. It highlights the importance of tracking public sentiment-ranging from fear to trust-to guide health messaging, inform policies, address misinformation, and encourage compliance with preventive measures during outbreaks. This study focuses on the use of sentiment analysis to understand public reactions to HMPV during the 2024 outbreak. The research applies advanced transformer models, particularly XLNet, achieving an accuracy of 93.50% in sentiment classification tasks. Additionally, We incorporate explainable AI (XAI) through SHAP to provide transparency in how the model identifies key factors influencing public sentiment.
abstract_zh: 中国发生的暴发(人偏肺病毒)疫情,随后传播至英国和其他国家,由于其对易感人群的潜在影响而引发了广泛关注。尽管人偏肺病毒通常只会引起轻微症状,但其对老年人和免疫功能低下人群的影响促使卫生部门强调预防措施。此外,持续监测如人偏肺病毒等呼吸道病毒仍然重要,因为新因素(如新出现的变种)可能会随时间改变其行为。这些因素导致了公众反应的分歧,一些人表现出焦虑,而另一些人则对病毒表现出漠视态度。本文探讨了情感分析如何通过分析YouTube等社交媒体平台的数据,增强我们对公众对人偏肺病毒反应的理解。文章强调了跟踪公众情感(从恐惧到信任)的重要性,以指导健康信息传播、制定政策、应对错误信息,并在暴发期间鼓励遵守预防措施。本研究聚焦于2024年暴发期间使用情感分析来理解公众对人偏肺病毒的反应。研究应用了先进的Transformer模型,特别是XLNet,在情感分类任务中实现了93.50%的准确率。此外,我们通过SHAP方法引入可解释AI(XAI),以提供模型如何识别影响公众情感的关键因素的透明度。

title: Bivalent RSVpreF Effectiveness Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)-Related Respiratory Disease Hospitalization and Emergency Department Visits Across Three RSV Seasons
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) protein subunit vaccines reduce the risk of severe outcomes such as hospitalization and emergency department (ED) visits for at least two RSV seasons following vaccination. No data have been published on real-world RSV vaccine effectiveness (VE) beyond the second season after vaccination. This study evaluates bivalent RSVpreF VE against RSV-related respiratory disease hospitalizations/ED visits throughout three seasons after vaccination. METHODS: This retrospective test-negative case-control study evaluates bivalent RSVpreF VE among adults aged ≥60 years at Kaiser Permanente Southern California, USA, with lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) or acute respiratory illness (ARI) over three RSV seasons (11/24/2023-4/18/2026). Cases were RSV-positive without coinfection. Controls were negative for RSV, hMPV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and positive for a non-vaccine preventable disease pathogen. Exposure was bivalent RSVpreF (Abrysvo) receipt ≥ 21 days before LRTD/ARI. Adjusted VE was estimated using odds ratios from multivariable logistic regression or generalized estimating equations. RESULTS: Overall adjusted VE against RSV-related LRTD hospitalization/ED visits was 80% (95% CI 68-87), 70% (95% CI 53-81), and 51% (95% CI -12-78) in the first, second, and third season after vaccination, respectively. Overall adjusted VE against RSV-related ARI hospitalization/ED visits was 81% (71-87), 64% (48-75), and 60% (15-81), respectively. Adjusted VE among non-immunocompromised individuals trended 4-7% higher than corresponding overall estimates. Overall adjusted VE across the three combined seasons was 73% (95% CI 64-80) and 73% (95% CI 65-79) against RSV-related LRTD and ARI, respectively. CONCLUSION: Bivalent RSVpreF provides protection against RSV-related respiratory hospitalization/ED visits for at least three seasons after vaccination in this population of older adults with a high prevalence of comorbidities. Estimates in the third season for ARI were more definitive, while those for LRTD were imprecise due to limited event numbers. This suggests bivalent RSVpreF vaccination results in substantial individual and public health benefit. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06077968.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性测试阴性病例对照研究评估了双价RSVpreF疫苗在60岁及以上美国加利福尼亚州凯撒医疗集团成人中对下呼吸道疾病(LRTD)或急性呼吸道疾病(ARI)的预防效果,研究覆盖了三个RSV季节(2023年11月24日至2026年4月18日)。
analysis_zh.methods: 病例为RSV阳性且无合并感染,对照组为RSV、hMPV、流感、SARS-CoV-2阴性,但对非疫苗可预防的疾病病原体阳性。暴露为在LRTD/ARI发生前至少21天接种双价RSVpreF(Abrysvo)。使用多变量逻辑回归或广义估计方程的比值比(OR)估计调整后的有效性(VE)。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在疫苗接种后第一、第二和第三RSV季节中,针对RSV相关LRTD住院/急诊科就诊的调整后VE分别为80%(95% CI 68-87)、70%(95% CI 53-81)和51%(95% CI -12-78)。针对RSV相关ARI住院/急诊科就诊的调整后VE分别为81%(71-87)、64%(48-75)和60%(15-81)。非免疫缺陷个体的调整后VE比总体估计高出4-7%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在具有高患病率合并症的老年人群中,双价RSVpreF在疫苗接种后至少三个RSV季节内提供了对RSV相关呼吸道住院/急诊科就诊的保护。第三季ARI的估计更为明确,而LRTD的估计因事件数量有限而不够精确。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究表明,双价RSVpreF 疫苗接种在个体和公共卫生层面带来了显著的益处。这些发现可能为未来疫苗的研发和针对老年人RSV预防的公共卫生策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究是一项回顾性测试阴性病例对照研究,可能会引入偏倚。由于第三季LRTD估计的不精确性以及潜在的混杂因素,证据强度为中等。

title: Computational designing of multiepitope based vaccine (MEBV) candidate against human metapneumovirus (HMPV) using immunoinformatics approach
abstract: Abstract Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a paramyxoviridae family respiratory pathogen, which is closely related to respiratory syncytial virus. It produces the symptoms of the flu and it may result in the serious damage of the airways and even though it is a worldwide problem, there is no vaccine available as yet. Three antigenic proteins namely surface glycoprotein, nucleoprotein and phosphoprotein were screened from all the receptors and showed no similarity to host genome. The three viral proteins were then screened for identifying the cytotoxic and helper T cell lymphocytes as well as linear and conformational B-cell lymphocytes. The vaccine had 13 MHC-I epitopes, one MHC-II epitope, and four linear B-cell epitopes, which were combined with linkers and beta-defensin as adjuvant into a 296-amino-acid MEBV with antigenicity score of 0.6644. Molecular docking and MD simulations showed that there is a high degree of interaction with human TLR3 with binding energy of − 14.6 and immune activation. Moreover, the disulfide engineering enhanced construct stability. Cloning and codon optimization was used to verify efficient expression in the target host. Taken together, these findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen of HMPV.

It produces the symptoms of the flu and it may result in the serious damage of the airways and even though it is a worldwide problem, there is no vaccine available as yet. Three antigenic proteins namely surface glycoprotein, nucleoprotein and phosphoprotein were screened from all the receptors and showed no similarity to host genome. The three viral proteins were then screened for identifying the cytotoxic and helper T cell lymphocytes as well as linear and conformational B-cell lymphocytes. The vaccine had 13 MHC-I epitopes, one MHC-II epitope, and four linear B-cell epitopes, which were combined with linkers and beta-defensin as adjuvant into a 296-amino-acid MEBV with antigenicity score of 0.6644. Molecular docking and MD simulations showed that there is a high degree of interaction with human TLR3 with binding energy of − 14.6 and immune activation. Moreover, the disulfide engineering enhanced construct stability. Cloning and codon optimization was used to verify efficient expression in the target host. Taken together, these findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen of HMPV.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to design a multiepitope based vaccine (MEBV) candidate against human metapneumovirus (HMPV) using immunoinformatics approach, as HMPV is a respiratory pathogen closely related to respiratory syncytial virus and causes flu-like symptoms with potential for serious airway damage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved computational designing of a vaccine candidate against HMPV, focusing on antigenic proteins and their interactions with immune cells. The research was conducted using immunoinformatics methods and targeted the development of a vaccine for HMPV.
analysis.methods: The researchers used computational methods to screen three antigenic proteins from HMPV, identified epitopes for T and B cell responses, combined them with linkers and beta-defensin as an adjuvant, and performed molecular docking and MD simulations to assess interactions with human TLR3.
analysis.main_results: The MEBV candidate was composed of 13 MHC-I epitopes, one MHC-II epitope, and four linear B-cell epitopes, resulting in a 296-amino-acid construct with an antigenicity score of 0.6644. Molecular docking and MD simulations showed a high degree of interaction with human TLR3, with binding energy of −14.6 and immune activation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen for HMPV, offering a novel approach to vaccine development through immunoinformatics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further research into HMPV vaccine development, which could lead to improved surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies for HMPV-related respiratory infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to computational methods and does not include experimental validation, which may affect the strength of the evidence. However, the use of molecular docking and MD simulations provides a moderate level of confidence in the vaccine's potential.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a computational approach to designing a multiepitope based vaccine (MEBV) candidate against human metapneumovirus (HMPV). HMPV, a paramyxoviridae family respiratory pathogen, causes flu-like symptoms and can lead to serious airway damage, yet no vaccine exists. The researchers identified three antigenic proteins from HMPV and screened them for epitopes that could elicit immune responses. These epitopes were combined with linkers and beta-defensin as an adjuvant to create a 296-amino-acid MEBV with an antigenicity score of 0.6644. Molecular docking and MD simulations demonstrated a high degree of interaction with human TLR3, with binding energy of −14.6 and immune activation. Disulfide engineering was used to enhance construct stability, and cloning and codon optimization were performed to verify efficient expression in the target host. The findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen for HMPV, offering a novel approach to vaccine development. The study's results could inform future research into HMPV vaccine development, potentially improving surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies. However, the study is limited to computational methods and lacks experimental validation, which may affect the strength of the evidence, though the use of molecular docking and MD simulations provides a moderate level of confidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用免疫信息学方法设计一种基于多表位的疫苗(MEBV)候选物,以对抗人偏肺病毒(HMPV)。因为HMPV是一种与呼吸道合胞病毒密切相关、可引起流感样症状并可能导致严重气道损伤的呼吸道病原体。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及使用计算方法设计一种针对HMPV的疫苗候选物,重点研究抗原蛋白及其与免疫细胞的相互作用。研究采用免疫信息学方法,目标是开发一种针对HMPV的疫苗。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用计算方法从HMPV中筛选出三种抗原蛋白,识别T细胞和B细胞免疫应答的表位,将这些表位与连接子和β-防御素作为佐剂结合,并进行分子对接和分子动力学模拟以评估其与人类TLR3的相互作用。
elements_zh.main_results: MEBV候选物由13个MHC-I表位、1个MHC-II表位和4个线性B细胞表位组成,形成一个296个氨基酸的构建体,其抗原性评分为0.6644。分子对接和分子动力学模拟显示,该MEBV与人类TLR3有高度的相互作用,结合能为−14.6,并具有免疫激活作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,所提出的MEBV具有作为HMPV免疫原的潜力,通过免疫信息学方法为疫苗开发提供了一种新颖的途径。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为进一步研究HMPV 疫苗开发奠定了基础,可能有助于改进监测、诊断以及HMPV相关呼吸道感染的预防策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于计算方法,未包括实验验证,这可能影响证据的强度。然而,使用分子对接和分子动力学模拟为疫苗的潜力提供了中等程度的信心。

analysis_en.main_results: The MEBV candidate was composed of 13 MHC-I epitopes, one MHC-II epitope, and four linear B-cell epitopes, resulting in a 296-amino-acid construct with an antigenicity score of 0.6644. Molecular docking and MD simulations showed a high degree of interaction with human TLR3, with binding energy of −14.6 and immune activation.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen for HMPV, offering a novel approach to vaccine development through immunoinformatics.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide a foundation for further research into HMPV vaccine development, which could lead to improved surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies for HMPV-related respiratory infections.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to computational methods and does not include experimental validation, which may affect the strength of the evidence. However, the use of molecular docking and MD simulations provides a moderate level of confidence in the vaccine's potential.

title_zh: 基于计算设计的多表位疫苗(MEBV)候选物用于针对人偏肺病毒(HMPV)的免疫信息学方法
source_body_en: Abstract Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a paramyxoviridae family respiratory pathogen, which is closely related to respiratory syncytial virus. It produces the symptoms of the flu and it may result in the serious damage of the airways and even though it is a worldwide problem, there is no vaccine available as yet. Three antigenic proteins namely surface glycoprotein, nucleoprotein and phosphoprotein were screened from all the receptors and showed no similarity to host genome. The three viral proteins were then screened for identifying the cytotoxic and helper T cell lymphocytes as well as linear and conformational B-cell lymphocytes. The vaccine had 13 MHC-I epitopes, one MHC-II epitope, and four linear B-cell epitopes, which were combined with linkers and beta-defensin as adjuvant into a 296-amino-acid MEBV with antigenicity score of 0.6644. Molecular docking and MD simulations showed that there is a high degree of interaction with human TLR3 with binding energy of − 14.6 and immune activation. Moreover, the disulfide engineering enhanced construct stability. Cloning and codon optimization was used to verify efficient expression in the target host. Taken together, these findings suggest that the proposed MEBV has potential as an immunogen of HMPV.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种副粘病毒科的呼吸道病原体,与呼吸道合胞病毒密切相关。它会产生流感样症状,并可能导致严重的气道损伤。尽管HMPV是一个全球性问题,但目前尚无疫苗可用。从所有受体中筛选出三种抗原蛋白,即表面糖蛋白、核蛋白和磷酸蛋白,且它们与宿主、基因组无相似性。随后,这三种病毒蛋白被筛选以识别细胞毒性T细胞和辅助T细胞淋巴细胞以及线性与构象性B细胞淋巴细胞。该疫苗包含13个MHC-I表位、1个MHC-II表位和4个线性B细胞表位,这些表位通过连接子和β-防御素作为佐剂组合成一个296个氨基酸的MEBV,其抗原性评分为0.6644。分子对接和分子动力学模拟显示,该MEBV与人类TLR3有高度的相互作用,结合能为−14.6,并具有免疫激活作用。此外,二硫键工程增强了构建体的稳定性。通过克隆和密码子优化验证了在目标宿主宿主中高效表达的潜力。综上所述,这些发现表明所提出的MEBV具有作为HMPV免疫原的潜力。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用免疫信息学方法设计一种基于多表位的疫苗(MEBV)候选物,以对抗人偏肺病毒(HMPV)。因为HMPV是一种与呼吸道合胞病毒密切相关、可引起流感样症状并可能导致严重气道损伤的呼吸道病原体。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及使用计算方法设计一种针对HMPV的疫苗候选物,重点研究抗原蛋白及其与免疫细胞的相互作用。研究采用免疫信息学方法,目标是开发一种针对HMPV的疫苗。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用计算方法从HMPV中筛选出三种抗原蛋白,识别T细胞和B细胞免疫应答的表位,将这些表位与连接子和β-防御素作为佐剂结合,并进行分子对接和分子动力学模拟以评估其与人类TLR3的相互作用。
analysis_zh.main_results: MEBV候选物由13个MHC-I表位、1个MHC-II表位和4个线性B细胞表位组成,形成一个296个氨基酸的构建体,其抗原性评分为0.6644。分子对接和分子动力学模拟显示,该MEBV与人类TLR3有高度的相互作用,结合能为−14.6,并具有免疫激活作用。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,所提出的MEBV具有作为HMPV免疫原的潜力,通过免疫信息学方法为疫苗开发提供了一种新颖的途径。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为进一步研究HMPV 疫苗开发奠定了基础,可能有助于改进监测、诊断以及HMPV相关呼吸道感染的预防策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于计算方法,未包括实验验证,这可能影响证据的强度。然而,使用分子对接和分子动力学模拟为疫苗的潜力提供了中等程度的信心。

title: Human metapneumovirus in central China, 2024–2025: epidemiology, co-infections, and temporal dynamics
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections in children, but comprehensive data from sentinel surveillance in the post‐pandemic period remain limited. Understanding its epidemiology and co‐infection patterns is critical for surveillance and prevention. We analyzed 36,143 respiratory specimens from ILI/SARI patients in Henan, China (2024–2025) using multiplex PCR for HMPV and 14 other pathogens. Positivity rates, enrichment ratios, co‐infection patterns, pathogen associations (OR/PR), and temporal dynamics (cross‐correlation and regression) were assessed. Overall HMPV positivity was 3.96% (1,432/36,143), with a sharp inter-year difference: 7.1% in 2024 vs. 1.7% in 2025, peaking at 26.2% during week 48. Children aged 3–5 years had the highest positivity (8.6%; enrichment ratio 2.18). Co-infections occurred in 56.2% of HMPV-positive cases, predominantly with Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. HMPV showed positive associations with these bacteria (OR = 2.01 and 1.47, respectively) but negative associations with influenza virus (OR = 0.20) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (OR = 0.17). HBoV also showed a positive association (OR = 1.66). RSV positivity at a 1-week lag had a positive effect on HMPV (β = 0.15, P = 0.048). HMPV was frequently detected in pediatric ILI/SARI patients during 2024–2025, with high rates of bacterial co‐detection. The temporal lead‐lag relationship with RSV underscores the need for integrated surveillance and age‐targeted prevention. The marked 2024 resurgence warrants continued monitoring to determine whether the observed patterns represent a short‐term anomaly or a sustained change in HMPV circulation.

title: Reduced expression of human metapneumovirus matrix protein impacts virus assembly and ribonucleoprotein localization
abstract: ABSTRACT Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes severe respiratory tract infections in all cohorts, particularly in vulnerable groups such as children, older adults, and the immunocompromised. The matrix (M) protein of HMPV, like the M proteins of other members of the order Mononegavirales , is involved in virus assembly and budding. However, other functions of the HMPV M protein have yet to be elucidated. To investigate the various functions of the M protein, we used a peptide-conjugated phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PPMO) antisense agent designed to block translation of the M gene during infection. Treatment with the PPMO targeted against M mRNA (PPMO M ) led to dose-dependent decreases in M expression, and a 10 μM PPMO M treatment applied at 1 hour post-infection (hpi) led to a >95% reduction in M protein at 24 hpi. Reductions in M expression had a significant impact on virus production and viral titers. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) probes used to detect vRNA showed that a reduction in M led to an increase in inclusion body (IB) count per cell, but a decrease in the average IB volume per cell at 12 and 24 hpi. HMPV-infected cells treated with PPMO M exhibited lower levels of phosphoprotein (P) at the plasma membrane. Importantly, no change in viral ribonucleoprotein movement (vRNP) was observed when the M protein levels were reduced. These studies support a model where the M protein does not facilitate movement, but instead is critical for the transfer to and stable association of vRNPs with the assembly sites at the membrane. IMPORTANCE Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a respiratory pathogen that can cause severe infections in humans, but there are no targeted treatment options for HMPV. To better characterize HMPV, a matrix (M) protein-targeted peptide-conjugated phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PPMO M ) was designed to control M expression during infection. Inhibition of M expression resulted in infections with reduced viral filaments and less viral RNA at the cell periphery. A reduction in M protein expression did not disrupt the active transport of viral ribonucleoproteins (vRNPs) but did significantly decrease vRNP localization at membranes and increase the number of inclusion bodies within infected cells. Viral titers were significantly reduced when M protein expression was inhibited, and dose-dependent reductions in M protein directly correlated with viral particle production. This study uses a unique tool to characterize the HMPV M protein during infection.

source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes severe respiratory tract infections in all cohorts, particularly in vulnerable groups such as children, older adults, and the immunocompromised. However, other functions of the HMPV M protein have yet to be elucidated. Importantly, no change in viral ribonucleoprotein movement (vRNP) was observed when the M protein levels were reduced. These studies support a model where the M protein does not facilitate movement, but instead is critical for the transfer to and stable association of vRNPs with the assembly sites at the membrane. IMPORTANCE Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a respiratory pathogen that can cause severe infections in humans, but there are no targeted treatment options for HMPV. To better characterize HMPV, a matrix (M) protein-targeted peptide-conjugated phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PPMO M ) was designed to control M expression during infection. Viral titers were significantly reduced when M protein expression was inhibited, and dose-dependent reductions in M protein directly correlated with viral particle production. This study uses a unique tool to characterize the HMPV M protein during infection.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 在所有 队列研究 中引起严重呼吸道感染,特别是在儿童、老年人和免疫功能低下等弱势群体中。HMPV 的基质 (M) 蛋白与单链病毒目其他成员的 M 蛋白一样,参与病毒组装和出芽。然而,HMPV M 蛋白的其他功能尚未阐明。为了研究 M 蛋白的各种功能,我们使用了肽缀合的磷酸二酰胺吗啉寡聚物 (PPMO) 反义剂,旨在阻断感染期间 M 基因的翻译。治疗 与针对 M mRNA (PPMO M ) 的 PPMO 导致 M 表达呈剂量依赖性下降,感染后 1 小时 (hpi) 应用 10 μM PPMO M 治疗 导致 24 hpi 时 M 蛋白减少 > 95%。M 表达的减少对病毒产生和病毒滴度有显着影响。用于检测 vRNA 的荧光原位杂交 (FISH) 探针显示,M 的减少导致每个细胞的包涵体 (IB) 计数增加,但在 12 和 24 hpi 时每个细胞的平均 IB 体积减少。用 PPMO M 处理的 HMPV 感染细胞在质膜上表现出较低水平的磷蛋白 (P)。重要的是,当 M 蛋白水平降低时,没有观察到病毒核糖核蛋白运动 (vRNP) 的变化。这些研究支持这样一种模型:M 蛋白并不促进运动,而是对于 vRNP 转移到膜上的组装位点并与膜上的组装位点稳定结合至关重要。重要性 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 是一种呼吸道病原体,可引起人类严重感染,但没有针对 HMPV 的针对性 治疗 选择。为了更好地表征 HMPV,设计了一种基质 (M) 蛋白靶向肽缀合的磷酸二酰胺吗啉寡聚物 (PPMO M ) 来控制感染期间的 M 表达。抑制 M 表达会导致感染时细胞外周病毒丝减少,病毒 RNA 减少。M蛋白表达的减少不会破坏病毒核糖核蛋白(vRNP)的主动运输,但会显着降低vRNP在膜上的定位并增加感染细胞内包涵体的数量。当 M 蛋白表达受到抑制时,病毒滴度显着降低,并且 M 蛋白的剂量依赖性降低与病毒颗粒的产生直接相关。本研究使用独特的工具来表征感染期间的 HMPV M 蛋白。

title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) as a significant respiratory pathogen affecting all age groups, especially young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. The evidence base includes a systematic literature review of peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies. Key conclusions highlight that HMPV primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that influence both viral clearance and disease progression. Investigational therapies, such as fusion and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Vaccine development is ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. The virus's ability to evade immune responses contributes to disease severity in vulnerable populations. The review identifies the need for improved diagnostics, public awareness, and targeted research to manage HMPV infections effectively. Controversies include the unproven efficacy of immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies, and the necessity for more clinical trials to establish safe and effective therapeutic options. Research and practice implications emphasize the importance of continued investigation into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines to address the public health challenge posed by HMPV.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 人偏肺病毒是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可引起所有年龄段人群的感染,尤其是在婴幼儿、免疫功能低下者和老年人中尤为突出。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 通过同行评审的期刊、临床试验和近期研究进行了系统文献综述,以聚焦人偏肺病毒感染。数据被提取并分析,以评估抗病毒药物疗法、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂以及疫苗候选药物的有效性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,引发免疫应答,这些反应既有助于病毒清除,也导致疾病发病机制。针对病毒的治疗药物,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但需要进一步验证。疫苗的发展正在进行中,已有几种候选药物进入临床前和早期临床阶段。由于缺乏针对性的治疗和疫苗,人偏肺病毒仍对公共卫生构成挑战。持续研究抗病毒药物药物、单克隆抗体和疫苗对于有效管理疾病至关重要。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 免疫调节药物和草药疗法可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的疗效尚未得到证实。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度,尤其是在易感人群中。需要进一步的临床试验以确定安全有效的治疗方案。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 改善诊断途径、公众意识和有针对性的研究对于控制 HMPV 感染至关重要。

title: Age-stratified clinical features and factors associated with severe pneumonia in hospitalized children with human metapneumovirus–associated lower respiratory tract infection
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children, yet age-stratified analyses across the full pediatric age range and the associations between pathogen co-detection and disease severity remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to delineate the age-related clinical features of hMPV-LRTI and identify factors associated with severe pneumonia. This retrospective study included children aged 0 to 6 years had the highest proportions of atelectasis (22.4%), unilateral involvement (65.7%), and severe pneumonia (31.0%). In the primary model, atelectasis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 47.52), underlying disease (9.49), consolidation (6.82), fever (3.29), wheezing (2.50), Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) co-detection (1.90), higher absolute neutrophil counts (1.47 per 5 × 109/L), and higher C-reactive protein levels (1.14 per 10 mg/L) were associated with higher odds; higher absolute monocyte counts (0.71 per 1 × 109/L) and bacterial co-detection (0.60) were associated with lower odds. The large radiological associations may partly reflect overlap with the extent-based severity criteria. MP co-detection increased from 6.0% in infants aged 0–6 months to 50.0% in children > 6 years. The overall age-group term did not reach statistical significance. Clinical and radiological manifestations of hMPV-LRTI varied across age groups. MP co-detection was more frequent in older children and was associated with higher odds of severe pneumonia after multivariable adjustment. These findings may inform age-specific clinical assessment, with attention to respiratory status in young infants and, in school-aged children, peri-admission chest imaging when clinically indicated and further clinical and microbiological evaluation when MP is co-detected.

abstract_original: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in children, yet age-stratified analyses across the full pediatric age range and the associations between pathogen co-detection and disease severity remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to delineate the age-related clinical features of hMPV-LRTI and identify factors associated with severe pneumonia. This retrospective study included children aged 0 to 6 years had the highest proportions of atelectasis (22.4%), unilateral involvement (65.7%), and severe pneumonia (31.0%). In the primary model, atelectasis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 47.52), underlying disease (9.49), consolidation (6.82), fever (3.29), wheezing (2.50), Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) co-detection (1.90), higher absolute neutrophil counts (1.47 per 5 × 109/L), and higher C-reactive protein levels (1.14 per 10 mg/L) were associated with higher odds; higher absolute monocyte counts (0.71 per 1 × 109/L) and bacterial co-detection (0.60) were associated with lower odds. The large radiological associations may partly reflect overlap with the extent-based severity criteria. MP co-detection increased from 6.0% in infants aged 0–6 months to 50.0% in children > 6 years. The overall age-group term did not reach statistical significance. Clinical and radiological manifestations of hMPV-LRTI varied across age groups. MP co-detection was more frequent in older children and was associated with higher odds of severe pneumonia after multivariable adjustment. These findings may inform age-specific clinical assessment, with attention to respiratory status in young infants and, in school-aged children, peri-admission chest imaging when clinically indicated and further clinical and microbiological evaluation when MP is co-detected.

title: Immunoinformatics-guided design and in silico evaluation of BAFF- and APRIL-adjuvanted multi-epitope vaccine candidates against human metapneumovirus
abstract: Introduction Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a leading cause of acute respiratory tract infections in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals; however, no licensed vaccine is currently available. This study employed an immunoinformatics-guided reverse vaccinology approach to design novel BAFF- and APRIL-adjuvanted multi-epitope vaccine candidates against HMPV. Methods Major structural and non-structural HMPV proteins, including fusion (F), attachment glycoprotein (G), (matrix) M2-1, M2-2, phosphoprotein (P), nucleoprotein (N), small hydrophobic (SH), and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (L) proteins, were screened for antigenicity. Cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), B-cell, and interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-inducing epitopes were predicted and evaluated for antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, and immunogenicity before being assembled into multi-epitope constructs using appropriate peptide linkers. BAFF and APRIL were incorporated as candidate immunomodulatory components based on their established roles in B-cell biology and humoral immune responses. Results The final vaccine constructs contained 24 selected epitopes (8 CTL, 8 HTL, and 8 B-cell epitopes) and demonstrated favorable predicted antigenicity, stability, hydrophilicity, thermostability, and non-allergenic and non-toxic properties. Secondary structure analysis revealed balanced proportions of α-helices, β-strands, and random coils, supporting structural stability and epitope accessibility. Molecular docking predicted putative interactions between the vaccine constructs and Toll-like receptors TLR1 and TLR4, with the predicted complexes exhibiting multiple intermolecular contacts at the receptor-ligand interfaces. These findings suggest structural compatibility between the vaccine constructs and the selected TLRs; however, functional receptor binding and activation require experimental validation. Conclusion The in silico analyses identified BAFF- and APRIL-containing multi-epitope constructs with favorable predicted antigenic, physicochemical, structural, and immunological characteristics that warrant further experimental investigation. These computational findings provide a basis for prioritizing candidate constructs. Nevertheless, molecular dynamics simulations and in vitro and in vivo studies are required to validate the structural stability, immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy of the proposed vaccine candidates.

analysis.main_results: The final vaccine constructs contained 24 selected epitopes (8 CTL, 8 HTL, and 8 B-cell epitopes) and demonstrated favorable predicted antigenicity, stability, hydrophilicity, thermostability, and non-allergenic and non-toxic properties.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These computational findings provide a basis for prioritizing candidate constructs that may inform future experimental investigations into vaccine development for HMPV.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the lack of a licensed vaccine for human metapneumovirus (HMPV) by employing an immunoinformatics-guided reverse vaccinology approach. The researchers identified and assembled 24 epitopes from major HMPV proteins into multi-epitope constructs, which were evaluated for antigenicity, stability, hydrophilicity, thermostability, and non-allergenic and non-toxic properties. The results indicated favorable predicted characteristics of the vaccine constructs, suggesting structural compatibility with Toll-like receptors TLR1 and TLR4. However, the authors emphasized that functional receptor binding and activation require experimental validation. The study's computational findings offer a foundation for further experimental investigation into vaccine development for HMPV. While the in silico approach provides valuable insights, additional studies are necessary to confirm the constructs' immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on computational models without experimental validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是婴幼儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群急性呼吸道感染的主要病原体;然而目前尚无获批的疫苗疫苗。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用基于免疫信息学的反向疫苗学方法设计新型BAFF和APRIL佐剂多表位疫苗候选疫苗以针对HMPV。

Cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), B-cell, and interferon-γ (IFN-γ)-inducing epitopes were predicted and evaluated for antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, and immunogenicity before being assembled into multi-epitope constructs using appropriate peptide linkers. BAFF and APRIL were incorporated as candidate immunomodulatory components based on their established roles in B-cell biology and humoral immune responses. Results The final vaccine constructs contained 24 selected epitopes (8 CTL, 8 HTL, and 8 B-cell epitopes) and demonstrated favorable predicted antigenicity, stability, hydrophilicity, thermostability, and non-allergenic and non-toxic properties. Secondary structure analysis revealed balanced proportions of α-helices, β-strands, and random coils, supporting structural stability and epitope accessibility. Molecular docking predicted putative interactions between the vaccine constructs and Toll-like receptors TLR1 and TLR4, with the predicted complexes exhibiting multiple intermolecular contacts at the receptor-ligand interfaces. These findings suggest structural compatibility between the vaccine constructs and the selected TLRs; however, functional receptor binding and activation require experimental validation. Conclusion The in silico analyses identified BAFF- and APRIL-containing multi-epitope constructs with favorable predicted antigenic, physicochemical, structural, and immunological characteristics that warrant further experimental investigation. These computational findings provide a basis for prioritizing candidate constructs. Nevertheless, molecular dynamics simulations and in vitro and in vivo studies are required to validate the structural stability, immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy of the proposed vaccine candidates.
abstract_zh: 引言 人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是婴幼儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群急性呼吸道感染的主要病原体;然而目前尚无获批的疫苗疫苗。本研究采用基于免疫信息学的反向疫苗学方法设计新型BAFF和APRIL佐剂多表位疫苗候选疫苗以针对HMPV。方法 对主要的HMPV结构蛋白和非结构蛋白,包括融合蛋白(F)、附着糖蛋白(G)、(基质)M2-1、M2-2、磷酸蛋白(P)、核蛋白(N)、小疏水蛋白(SH)和RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶(L)蛋白进行了抗原性筛选。预测并评估了细胞毒性T淋巴细胞(CTL)、辅助T淋巴细胞(HTL)、B细胞和干扰素-γ(IFN-γ)诱导表位的抗原性、致敏性、毒性及免疫原性,随后使用适当的肽连接子将其组装成多表位结构。基于其在B细胞生物学和体液免疫中的已知作用,将BAFF和APRIL作为候选免疫调节成分纳入其中。结果 最终的疫苗结构包含24个选定的表位(8个CTL表位、8个HTL表位和8个B细胞表位),并表现出良好的预测抗原性、稳定性、亲水性、热稳定性以及非致敏性和非毒性特性。二级结构分析显示α-螺旋、β-折叠和无规卷曲的比例均衡,支持结构稳定性和表位可接近性。分子对接预测了疫苗结构与Toll样受体TLR1和TLR4之间的潜在相互作用,预测的复合物在受体-配体界面表现出多个分子间接触。这些发现表明疫苗结构与所选TLRs之间存在结构兼容性;然而,功能性受体结合和激活仍需实验验证。结论 体外分析识别出含有BAFF和APRIL的多表位结构,其预测的抗原性、物理化学特性、结构特性和免疫特性均良好,值得进一步实验研究。这些计算结果为候选结构的优先级提供了依据。然而,需要进行分子动力学模拟以及体外和体内研究,以验证所提出疫苗候选疫苗的结构稳定性、免疫原性、安全性和保护效果。

title: Retrospective analysis of multiplex panel tests in the diagnosis of respiratory tract infections
abstract: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) remain a major global health concern, particularly in children. The overlapping clinical manifestations of RTIs highlight the need for rapid and accurate diagnostic methods such as multiplex PCR (mPCR). This retrospective single-center study investigated the epidemiology of respiratory pathogens detected by mPCR, focusing on their distribution, age-related patterns, seasonal variation, and coinfections. Nasopharyngeal swab samples from 328 patients with suspected acute RTIs, collected between January 2022 and December 2023, were analyzed using the BioFire FilmArray Respiratory Panel 2.1. Demographic characteristics, clinical findings, pathogen distribution, seasonal trends, and coinfections were evaluated. At least one respiratory pathogen was detected in 270 of 328 specimens, yielding an overall positivity rate of 82.3%. Viral pathogens predominated; human rhinovirus/enterovirus HRV/HEV (28%), adenovirus (21.8%), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (14.2%), and influenza viruses (11.3%) were the most frequently identified agents. The results showed that 82.3% of specimens tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen, with viral agents being the most frequently identified. abstract_zh: 呼吸道感染(RTIs)仍然是全球主要的健康问题,尤其是在儿童中。RTIs的重叠临床表现凸显了需要快速准确的诊断方法,如多重PCR(mPCR)。本回顾性单中心研究调查了mPCR检测到的呼吸道病原体的种类,重点关注其分布、年龄相关模式、季节性变化和混合感染。使用BioFire FilmArray Respiratory Panel 2.1对2022年1月至2023年12月期间收集的328例疑似急性RTI患者的鼻咽拭子样本进行了分析。评估了人口统计学特征、临床发现、病原体分布、季节趋势和混合感染情况。在328份样本中,至少检测到一种呼吸道病原体的有270份,总体阳性率为82.3%。病毒性病原体占主导地位;人类鼻病毒/肠病毒HRV/HEV(28%)、腺病毒(21.8%)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)(14.2%)和流感病毒(11.3%)是最常见的病原体。严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)和人偏肺病毒(HMPV)分别在6.8%和5.8%的病例中被检测到。绝大多数样本(91.5%)来自0-18岁儿童。在阳性病例中,有31.8%出现了混合感染,最常见的混合感染涉及腺病毒和HRV/HEV。季节性分析显示,在冬季和春季的阳性率显著增加,占所有阳性病例的74%。细菌性病原体很少被检测到。mPCR表现出高诊断价值,检测到病原体的样本占82.3%,主要为病毒性病原体。这些发现支持了mPCR在提高诊断准确性并提供有价值的区域流行病学数据中的作用。快速识别病毒性病原体可能也有助于抗菌药物的合理使用,通过促进更明智的临床决策;然而,本研究中并未评估抗生素的使用情况。

title: Post-pandemic re-establishment of respiratory virus seasonality and molecular epidemiology of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus in Northern Italy: a three-year surveillance study (2023-2026).
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory virus circulation progressively returned towards patterns observed in the pre-pandemic period. However, long-term epidemiological data describing the re-establishment of respiratory viral seasonality and the molecular diversity of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus (RV/EV) remain limited. METHODS: To investigate the circulation patterns of respiratory viruses and characterize the RV/EV in Northern Italy, a retrospective observational study was conducted on samples collected between April 2023 and April 2026 at Brescia Civic Hospital. Respiratory viruses were detected by real-time PCR, and RV/EV-positive samples were characterized through next-generation sequencing. RESULTS: A total of 6,919 respiratory virus-positive samples were identified. SARS-CoV-2 remained the most frequently detected pathogen, followed by RV/EV, influenza A/B (FLU A/B), adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus, bocavirus, and human metapneumovirus. Distinct seasonal peaks were observed for FLU A/B and RSV during winter months, whereas RV/EV circulated continuously throughout the year. Molecular characterization of 224 RV/EV-positive samples revealed substantial genetic diversity. Pediatric patients accounted for the majority of sequenced cases. CONCLUSIONS: Three years after the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory viruses have re-established their characteristic seasonal circulation patterns. Nevertheless, RV/EV remain the dominant non-influenza respiratory pathogens and display considerable genetic heterogeneity. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for early detection of emerging respiratory viral threats.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory virus circulation progressively returned towards patterns observed in the pre-pandemic period. However, long-term epidemiological data describing the re-establishment of respiratory viral seasonality and the molecular diversity of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus (RV/EV) remain limited.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: To investigate the circulation patterns of respiratory viruses and characterize the RV/EV in Northern Italy, a retrospective observational study was conducted on samples collected between April 2023 and April 2026 at Brescia Civic Hospital.
analysis_en.methods: Respiratory viruses were detected by real-time PCR, and RV/EV-positive samples were characterized through next-generation sequencing.
analysis_en.main_results: A total of 6,919 respiratory virus-positive samples were identified. SARS-CoV-2 remained the most frequently detected pathogen, followed by RV/EV, influenza A/B (FLU A/B), adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus, bocavirus, and human metapneumovirus. Distinct seasonal peaks were observed for FLU A/B and RSV during winter months, whereas RV/EV circulated continuously throughout the year. Molecular characterization of 224 RV/EV-positive samples revealed substantial genetic diversity. Pediatric patients accounted for the majority of sequenced cases.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Three years after the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory viruses have re-established their characteristic seasonal circulation patterns. Nevertheless, RV/EV remain the dominant non-influenza respiratory pathogens and display considerable genetic heterogeneity.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for early detection of emerging respiratory viral threats.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the retrospective nature of the study and the focus on a single hospital, which may limit generalizability. However, the substantial genetic diversity observed in RV/EV highlights the importance of ongoing surveillance.

title_zh: 后疫情时代北意大利呼吸道病毒季节性恢复及鼻病毒/肠病毒分子 流行病学:一项为期三年的 监测 研究(2023-2026)
source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory virus circulation progressively returned towards patterns observed in the pre-pandemic period. However, long-term epidemiological data describing the re-establishment of respiratory viral seasonality and the molecular diversity of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus (RV/EV) remain limited. METHODS: To investigate the circulation patterns of respiratory viruses and characterize the RV/EV in Northern Italy, a retrospective observational study was conducted on samples collected between April 2023 and April 2026 at Brescia Civic Hospital. Respiratory viruses were detected by real-time PCR, and RV/EV-positive samples were characterized through next-generation sequencing. RESULTS: A total of 6,919 respiratory virus-positive samples were identified. SARS-CoV-2 remained the most frequently detected pathogen, followed by RV/EV, influenza A/B (FLU A/B), adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus, bocavirus, and human metapneumovirus. Distinct seasonal peaks were observed for FLU A/B and RSV during winter months, whereas RV/EV circulated continuously throughout the year. Molecular characterization of 224 RV/EV-positive samples revealed substantial genetic diversity. Pediatric patients accounted for the majority of sequenced cases. CONCLUSIONS: Three years after the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory viruses have re-established their characteristic seasonal circulation patterns. Nevertheless, RV/EV remain the dominant non-influenza respiratory pathogens and display considerable genetic heterogeneity. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for early detection of emerging respiratory viral threats.

title: Avian metapneumovirus infections in poultry flocks in Poland – molecular evidence for emerging divergence from vaccine strains
abstract: Despite use of aMPV vaccines, clinical signs of disease caused by aMPV infection with field strains were widely reported in poultry production in Poland.The strains detected formed a distinct cluster of "Polish field strains".Two complete aMPV-B genomes revealed several non-synonymous mutations, especially in G and SH genes, that may account for the poor protection provided by the vaccines.Phylogenetic analysis of two Polish complete genomes revealed a significant genetic distance from available aMPV-B strains.

title: Burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) hospitalizations among adults aged 60 years or more in Brazil: A retrospective surveillance database analysis (2013-2024).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Globally, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in adults aged ≥60 years. Risk increases with advancing age and comorbidities, particularly cardiopulmonary disease and diabetes. RSV disease burden in adults is often underestimated due to non-specific presentation and limited testing. In Brazil, RSV is a recognized driver of hospitalizations and deaths in older adults, yet comprehensive epidemiological data remain scarce. Here, we describe RSV-associated severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) hospitalizations among adults aged ≥60 years in Brazil between 2013 and 2024. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed RSV-associated SARI hospitalizations reported to the national Influenza Epidemiological Surveillance Information System -Gripe. Outcomes included hospitalization frequency, in-hospital mortality, case fatality rates (CFRs), seasonality, healthcare resource utilization, and comorbidities. RESULTS: Between 2013 and 2024, 4,636 RSV-related hospitalizations occurred in adults aged ≥60 years, increasing sharply after the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2024). Hospitalization rates increased from 15 per 100,000 in 2024. Women accounted for most cases (59%), and hospitalizations were concentrated in the South and Southeast regions partly due to test availability. Risk increases with advancing age and comorbidities, particularly cardiopulmonary disease and diabetes. Comorbidities were present in 71% of cases, most commonly cardiovascular (65%) and diabetes (33%)were strongly associated with increased mortality and healthcare resource utilization. CONCLUSIONS: RSV poses a substantial and increasing burden among Brazilian adults aged ≥60 years, with a high CFR, prolonged hospitalizations, and intensive healthcare resource utilization. These findings highlight the need to strengthen RSV surveillance and discuss vaccination strategies for adults aged older in Brazil.

title: Development of a Non-Invasive Indirect ELISA for Detecting IgY Against a Novel Avian Metapneumovirus Subtype C in Egg Yolks of Laying Ducks
abstract: Avian metapneumovirus subtype C (aMPV/C) has re-emerged as a widespread pathogen in China, causing hydrosalpinx fluid syndrome (HFS) in laying ducks and resulting in substantial economic losses, highlighting the urgent need for a reliable immunological detection method. In the present study, a non-invasive indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (iELISA) was developed and optimized for detecting aMPV/C-specific immunoglobulin Y (IgY) in egg yolks of laying ducks, using purified novel aMPV/C as the coating antigen. Checkerboard titration established the optimal conditions as an antigen concentration of 1.25 μg/mL and an IgY dilution of 1:200. The cut-off value, determined by receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, was 0.3268, enabling a detection limit of 1:3200 for IgY antibodies. The assay showed no cross-reactivity with IgY positive for other duck pathogens, and both intra-assay and inter-assay coefficients of variation were less than 10%, demonstrating good specificity and reproducibility. Clinical evaluation of 151 duck egg yolk samples yielded an overall aMPV/C-specific IgY positivity rate of 58.3% (88/151). The concordance rate between the iELISA and an indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) was 97.8% (45/46). These results indicate that the established iELISA for detecting aMPV/C-specific IgY is a reliable and practical tool for large-scale detection of aMPV/C exposure in clinical duck egg yolk samples.

title: Compartment-Aware Benchmarking of Respiratory-Virus Transcriptomes for Nasal and Blood Host-Response Modules: A Computational Study.
abstract: Public respiratory-virus transcriptomes are valuable for studying host responses, but differences in tissue source, control definition, and study design can confound pooled analyses. We developed a compartment-aware computational workflow to determine whether reproducible host-response activity can be identified while preserving nasal and blood biological context. The paired GSE117827 paediatric cohort served as the anchor dataset, comprising nasal-swab and whole-blood transcriptomes from symptomatic picornavirus infection, symptomatic respiratory syncytial virus infection, asymptomatic picornavirus detection, and virus-negative controls. After HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (HGNC) filtering, 27,685 genes were analyzed. Separate 50-gene protein-coding nasal and blood modules were defined from the top positive responses and locked before external evaluation. Gene-level nasal and blood effects were nearly independent (Pearson r = 0.015), and the modules shared six exploratory rank-overlap genes (Jaccard index = 0.064). Nevertheless, the nasal module separated infection from controls in independent upper-airway cohorts, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.749, 0.693, and 0.609, whereas the blood module achieved AUROCs of 0.832, 0.924, and 0.870 in external blood cohorts. In longitudinal natural-infection data, matched scores decreased from acute illness to discharge, with paired deltas of 0.436 for nasal samples and 0.330 for blood. Three additional benchmark datasets comprising 666 external samples, together with random-gene nulls, module-size sweeps, bootstrap stability, marker-program correlations, and variance partitioning, defined the robustness and limitations of the workflow. The Pandya 33-messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) set remained stronger for viral-versus-bacterial discrimination, while the blood module also increased in bacterial pneumonia. These findings support compartment-specific modules as reusable host-response activity scores for cohort comparison and recovery tracking, rather than universal pan-tissue biomarkers or stand-alone pathogen classifiers.

title: Trends and estimated costs of hospitalizations potentially associated with respiratory syncytial virus among children in Brazil, 2014-2025

source_records.title: Trends and estimated costs of hospitalizations potentially associated with respiratory syncytial virus among children in Brazil, 2014-2025
Trends and estimated costs of hospitalizations potentially associated with respiratory syncytial virus among children in Brazil, 2014-2025

full_text: ABSTRACTBackground: Respiratory syncytial virus, a major cause of respiratory infections and hospitalizations in young children, especially bronchiolitis, is an important burden to the health system in Brazil. This study evaluated the trends, seasonality, and economic impact of hospitalizations associated with respiratory syncytial virus in Brazilian children.Methods: This study analyzed hospitalizations for acute bronchitis and bronchiolitis (International Code of Diseases-10 J20-J21) in Brazilian children <5 years of age from January 2014 and March 2025 using data from the Brazil’s Unified Health System. Annual trends were assessed with linear regression, while time series decomposition evaluated seasonality. Direct medical costs were adjusted for inflation and converted to international dollars (Int$). Pearson’s correlation coefficient was employed to analyze associations between length of stay and hospitalization cost. Results: A total of 727,808 hospitalizations were recorded, with 86.8% occurring in children under 5 years old. Hospitalizations increased by 307.8%, with marked declines in 2020 during the coronavirus disease-2019 pandemic and consistent seasonal peaks between March-June. Direct medical costs totaled Int$ 166.8 million, with 55.5% of expenditures after 2020. The mean cost per hospitalization increased by Int$ 21.48 between 2014-2024 (Int$ 118.16-139.64). Length of stay correlated moderately with cost (r = 0.55), particularly strongly in southeastern and southern Brazil. Conclusions: Our findings revealed distinct seasonal and regional patterns in hospitalizations and a post-pandemic increase in costs. The association between prolonged hospitalization and higher expenditures underscores the need for targeted, region-specific preventive strategies and timely clinical interventions, to reduce the growing economic burden on the system. METHODSStudy designThis study analyzed the trend in hospitalizations caused by RSV from 2014 to 2025 8 , estimating the direct medical costs based on monthly data grouped by Brazil’s geographical regions.The Brazilian macro-region (North, Northeast, Midwest, Southeast, and South) was used as the stratification variable, with data aggregated at the regional level by month of hospital admission and patient's region of residence.Data curationData were extracted on May 11 from the BUHS’s Hospital Information System (SIH) via the DATASUS TabNet tool using the filters “hospital morbidity” and “place of residence”, covering the timespan of January 2014 to March 2025 by region and federative unit 9 . The analysis included hospitalizations of children under 5 years of age (0-4 years), considering all admission types (elective or urgent) and care regime (public or private contracted to the BUHS). Hospitalizations financed exclusively by private health insurance or out-of-pocket payment are not recorded in SIH and are therefore not captured in this analysis. International Code of Diseases (ICD)-10 codes J20-J21 (bronchitis and bronchiolitis) were selected 10 . Case definition was based solely on ICD-10 administrative coding, without laboratory confirmation; therefore, RSV cannot be directly attributed to individual hospitalizations, and the term 'potentially associated with RSV' is used throughout to reflect this limitation. Data were exported as .csv files and processed using R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Viena, Áustria, for organization, cleaning, and aggregation to support the statistical and temporal analyses 9 , 10 . Data extracted for the period January-March 2025 were considered preliminary, as records from the last 6 months in SIH/DATASUS are subject to consolidation updates; these data though included in descriptive and cost analyses, should be cautiously interpreted.Time series analysis: hospitalization’s annual growth rateThe annual growth rate was estimated using a simple linear regression model (Equation 1): Y=β0+ β1X+ε (1) where Y is the number of monthly hospitalizations, X is time (in months), is the intercept, β1 is the mean monthly increase or decrease rate (annualized estimates in the Results were calculated as 12×β1), and ε is the error term.The analyses were conducted using the R software 11 , using the core packages (I) ggplot2 12 for graphical display, (II) dplyr 13 for data manipulation, (III) readxl 14 for reading Excel files, (IV) patchwork 15 for combining graphics, combination, and (V) lubridate 16 for date manipulation. The trend line from linear regression was automatically adjusted with the geom_smooth (method = “lm”) function in ggplot2 12 , which estimated the coefficients (β0 and β1) and illustrated the fitted line.Time series decompositionFollowing linear analysis, time series decomposition was performed 17 , 18 . Data were aggregated by month for each region and converted into time series objects (ts) in R software via the stats package 11 . Each series was assigned a monthly frequency (12 per year), spanning January 2014 to December 2024 (complete annual cycles; the three months of partial 2025 data were excluded from the decomposition to avoid distortion of the seasonal component, while descriptive and cost analyses include data through March 2025). The decomposition differentiated the trend, seasonal, and residual components. Seasonal factors were examined to characterize and validate temporal patterns. Decomposition was performed with the decompose function (stats package) 11 for each regional and national time series. Graphs were generated using the ggplot2 14 autoplot function and organized to emphasize regional disparities.Autocorrelation analysis 19 , 20 was employed to detect temporal dependencies and seasonality in Brazil and its regions, using the acf function from the stats package 11 . It measured correlations at different lags and graphs were generated through the ggAcf function (forecast package) 21 , to identify short-term dependencies and seasonal or cyclical patterns across time scales.Direct medical cost estimationDirect medical costs of hospitalizations caused by RSV were estimated for 2014-2025. Mean costs per hospitalization were calculated annually for Brazil and each of its five regions. Boxplots were generated using ggplot2 (geom_boxplot) 12 to illustrate the annual dispersion of mean hospitalization costs. Descriptive statistics, including standard deviation and variance of mean values, were calculated for each year and region using dplyr functions 13 .The correlation between mean length of stay and mean direct medical cost per hospitalization was estimated using the cor function (stats package) 11 . A simple linear regression model (lm function) was applied to assess the association between average length of stay (independent variable) and adjusted average cost per hospitalization (dependent variable), corrected for inflation and converted to international dollars (Int$) using the purchasing power parity (PPP) conversion factor of 2.524 BRL/Int$, as recommended by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development and the World Bank 22 , 23 . Pearson’s correlation coefficient was employed to measure the strength and direction of the linear relationship between mean length of stay and mean direct medical cost per hospital stay 24 , 25 . Scatter plots were generated for each region, with trend lines based on the fitted regression model using geom_point function to plot the scatter points and geom_smooth (method = “lm”) from ggplot2 14 to add the regression line. Correlation strength was interpreted according to conventional thresholds.Inflation adjustment and currency conversionTo ensure temporal comparability, hospitalization costs were adjusted for inflation using Brazil’s extended national consumer price index provided by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (SIDRA table 1737, national level) 26 . Monthly values were aggregated by calendar year, and the national average for 2024 was adopted as the reference base year.For international comparability, inflation-adjusted values were converted to Int$ using Brazil’s 2024 PPP conversion factor of 2.524 BRL/Int$, as published by the World Bank 23 . A fixed PPP factor was utilized to present the historical series in standardized purchasing power, reflecting the actual economic burden of hospitalization costs in Brazil. All PPP conversions were applied exclusively to inflation-adjusted BRL values, following international best practices 22 . Ethical considerationsThis study was approved by the research ethics committee of the Gonçalo Moniz Research Center (approval no. 6.929.375 and IORG0002090/OMB no. 0990-0279) and complied with the Brazilian National Health Council Resolution CNS no. 466/2012. The databases included anonymized information from the Hospital Information System and the Mortality Information System, accessed via TABWIN and TABNET platforms (DATASUS) under e-SIC protocols no. 25072.028465/2024-98 and no. 25072.017378/2024-13. Study designThis study analyzed the trend in hospitalizations caused by RSV from 2014 to 2025 8 , estimating the direct medical costs based on monthly data grouped by Brazil’s geographical regions.The Brazilian macro-region (North, Northeast, Midwest, Southeast, and South) was used as the stratification variable, with data aggregated at the regional level by month of hospital admission and patient's region of residence. RESULTSBetween January 2014 and March 2025, Brazil reported 727,808 hospitalizations for acute bronchitis and acute bronchiolitis; of these, 86.8% (n = 631,724/727,808) occurred in children < 5 years of age. From 2014 to 2024, total hospitalizations increased by 307.8% (Figure 1). The southeastern region showed the highest increase (135.9%), followed by the northeastern (67.9%), midwestern (48.9%), and southern (48.5%) regions; northern Brazil had the lowest increase (6.6%). There was a marked national decline in 2020, corresponding to the first year of the coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (Figure 1). FIGURE 1:Trend in hospitalizations for bronchitis and acute bronchiolitis by month and year of care (2014-2025). Source: Brazilian Ministry of Health 12 . Data for the last 6 months, subject to change. Overall, hospitalizations rose significantly (128,6%) from 3548 in July 2014 to 8110 in June 2023. Residuals reflected variations such as the abrupt decline at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic (-3293 in April 2020) and isolated spikes (1742 in June 2023), a trend present in all regions. Seasonality remained stable, with a consistent annual cycle across regions (Supplementary Figure 1). In the midwest region, hospitalizations increased by 207% (from 265 in July 2014 to 814 in September 2024), with a decrease of 489 cases in April 2020, potentially attributed to the pandemic. In the northeast, the trend rose 143% (from 715 to 1740), also with notable residuals in 2020. The north experienced a more modest growth (54%; from 331 to 511), with reductions in May 2020 (- 353) and increases in May 2023 (+ 383). In the southeast, hospitalizations increased 108% (from 1538 in July 2014 to 3205 in September 2024), with residuals reducing in April 2020 (- 2113) and growing in March 2023 (+ 1266). In the south, cases grew from 700 in January 2014 to 1290 in September 2024, with residuals declining in June 2020 (- 840) during the pandemic (Supplementary Figure 1). Autocorrelation analysis indicated a seasonality at lag 12 (ACF = 0.60) in Brazil. The southeast (0.60) and south (0.64) had the strongest annual seasonality, followed by the midwest (0.57) and northeast (0.59). The north showed a weaker pattern (0.52) (Supplementary Figure 2).Regional boxplots exhibited a consistent seasonality, with hospitalization peaks between March and June. April and May had the highest median values in most regions. Nationally, the peak occurred between March and July, suggesting a consolidated epidemic pattern. In the northeast, north, and midwest, hospitalizations increased from March to June. In the south and southeast, seasonality persisted longer, with elevated rates until mid-August. From August to December, all regions showed lower medians and interquartile ranges, expressing reduced hospitalization rates (Figure 2). FIGURE 2:Hospitalizations for bronchitis and acute bronchiolitis potentially associated with respiratory syncytial virus cases by month and year (2014-2025). Source: Brazilian Ministry of Health 12 .
